ov: Birds of prey of the eagle family, found on every continent except Antarctica. “True” hawks such as goshawks and sparrowhawks are woodland hunters with short, broad wings; in the US the name also covers the broad-winged buzzards.

why.p: Trained for falconry, which used to be called hawking, rather than kept as pets.

df: Live prey, often ambushed with a sudden dash from a hidden perch.

cf.tip: Eagles and hawks belong to the same family. “Eagle” marks the bigger species.
Hawks kill with their talons; falcons kill with a notch on the beak and have longer, pointed wings.

fx: Each hawk eye has two foveae, the patches of sharpest vision.
